prophage_amr_comobilization--3eb68b95.gist: Whether antibiotic-resistance genes sitting next to prophages (integrated viral DNA) impose a growth cost on their bacterial hosts was not tested, so the question stays open. The analysis was not run.

prophage_amr_comobilization--4cead8a0.gist: In bacterial genomes, antibiotic-resistance genes lying close to prophage (integrated virus) markers were slightly more often part of the variable accessory genome than distant ones, with 67.6% of nearby genes accessory versus 65.5% of distant genes.

prophage_amr_comobilization--7802d299.gist: In the most resistance-burdened bacterial species, over half (55.7%) of antibiotic-resistance gene instances sit on the same contigs as prophage marker genes, suggesting a frequent physical link between resistance and integrated phages.

prophage_amr_comobilization--f3c69b78.gist: In a survey of the full pangenome collection, more than half of bacterial species carry both antibiotic-resistance genes and prophage (integrated virus) markers, 52.9% of the species. Prophage markers were mostly accessory, so they vary between strains of a species.

pseudomonas_carbon_ecology--0211e0cd.gist: In free-living Pseudomonas, carbon-use profiles carry real ecological signal, but the test was inconclusive on whether they can tell fine-grained environment types apart. Carbon metabolism alone, as measured here, does not settle a species' specific habitat.

pseudomonas_carbon_ecology--24adcf2d.gist: Rhamnose and fucose pathways looked more complete in Pseudomonas aeruginosa genomes (66.8%) than in the P. fluorescens group (41.3% and 45.1%). The comparison was inconclusive, so whether these lineages truly differ in pathway completeness remains unsettled.
pseudomonas_carbon_ecology--24adcf2d.title: Rhamnose and fucose pathways look more complete in P. aeruginosa, inconclusively

pseudomonas_carbon_ecology--9c42f41a.gist: Across Pseudomonas genomes, the P. aeruginosa group appears to have lost most of the ability to catabolize plant-derived sugars, while the P. fluorescens/putida group keeps it. Genome-based pathway predictions separated the two groups in 43 carbon pathways.

pseudomonas_carbon_ecology--a6ba828d.gist: In Pseudomonas genomes, the P. aeruginosa group has no complete pathways for xylose, arabinose or myo-inositol, whereas the P. fluorescens group often does, with ribose, galacturonate, mannitol and sorbitol also much lower. This suggests the groups use plant-derived sugars differently.

pseudomonas_carbon_ecology--cbe7e256.gist: In Pseudomonas, the carbon-use pathways encoded in a genome carry some signal about where a species lives. A classifier sorting species into soil, freshwater, plant-surface or rhizosphere habitats did clearly better than chance, suggesting carbon metabolism partly tracks habitat.

pseudomonas_carbon_ecology--eb1d58ae.gist: Across 54 free-living and plant-associated Pseudomonas species, the mix of carbon-use pathways in their genomes tracked where the strains were isolated, suggesting that carbon metabolism carries an ecological signal.

soil_frontier_genomics--0fa73728.gist: Models predicting functional-gene counts in soils from soil and climate, geochemical, or industrial variables all did worse than guessing the average on held-out samples. This test was inconclusive about whether these soil genes are predictable from such variables.

soil_frontier_genomics--25df967c.gist: Soil areas that are poorly represented in public genomic databases were more alkaline than well-mapped areas, by about 0.8 pH units. This suggests alkaline soil microbiomes are systematically under-sampled in public genomic databases.

soil_frontier_genomics--2ab586c6.gist: Forest and Cropland soils stand out as the least-mapped genomic frontier, with the highest genomic discovery index of the biomes compared, while Grassland and Wetland look relatively well mapped. This suggests where new soil sequencing could add the most.

soil_metal_functional_genomics--129a64ad.gist: In soil microbial communities, the abundance of many gene families shifted with metal levels, with chromium and lead giving the strongest signals. Transporter genes (ABC, RND) and biosynthesis genes dominated the top hits, suggesting soil microbial functions track metal contamination.

soil_metal_functional_genomics--2a80fc76.gist: Across soils matched to nearby KBase genomes, genes for cell division and nucleotide transport were enriched with copper, while energy-production genes were depleted. This suggests microbial communities under copper stress may trade energy metabolism for other functions.

soil_metal_functional_genomics--aaafa6a8.gist: In this soil study of metal concentrations and community functional genes, the share of gene-content variation explained by metals alone was not reported. This is missing data, so how strongly metals shape functional genes by themselves is unknown.

soil_metal_functional_genomics--becb7d4e.gist: Across soil, marine and wastewater microbial communities, the links between metal levels and gene functional categories differed by environment, suggesting each habitat responds to metals in its own way rather than through one shared resistance programme.

soil_metal_functional_genomics--e27860e8.gist: A soil study links metal concentrations to shifts in gene functional categories across 2,355 associations. How large each shift is has not been reported across the whole set, so many may be too small to matter biologically; this analysis was not performed.
soil_metal_functional_genomics--e27860e8.title: Size of metal-gene associations not yet systematically reported across the full set

soil_metal_functional_genomics--fd9b94cc.gist: In soil microbial communities, metal concentrations accounted for 80% of the variation in community gene-function profiles once differences between sampling projects were removed, suggesting metals strongly shape which functional genes communities carry.

t4ss_cazy_environmental_hgt--44ad24db.gist: Among environmental genomes assembled from metagenomes, those carrying a GT2 sugar-transferase gene near type IV secretion genes had 11× more metal resistance genes than other genomes. This suggests a link between gene-transfer machinery and metal tolerance.

t4ss_cazy_environmental_hgt--5d73bfde.gist: Scans of bacterial genomes found no detectable plasmid-borne carbohydrate-active enzyme genes among the top gene accumulators. Genomes with type IV secretion systems had 10× higher density of mobile genetic elements, suggesting these genes spread by chromosomal, integrative transfer.

t4ss_cazy_environmental_hgt--91e33b0b.gist: Across bacterial genomes, 92 families of carbohydrate-processing enzymes tend to sit near type IV secretion system genes, suggesting a link between secretion machinery and sugar-modifying enzymes. Glycosyltransferase family GT2 is the strongest association, found beside these loci in many genomes.

t4ss_cazy_environmental_hgt--a2b33180.gist: A gene-family tree for GT2 sugar-building enzymes points to 32 high-confidence horizontal gene transfer events crossing phyla, suggesting these genes move between distant bacterial lineages, with the strongest event linking many phyla.

t4ss_cazy_environmental_hgt--a744bbc9.gist: Genes for type IV secretion and conjugation, a machinery bacteria use to pass DNA between cells, turned up in 21.8% of high-quality environmental genomes assembled from metagenomes, suggesting DNA-transfer capacity is widespread in environmental bacteria.

truly_dark_genes--8c818410.gist: Truly dark genes (no known function even after modern annotation) that strongly affect growth in gene-knockout screens showed no detectable stress enrichment. They were less often stress-related than genes whose annotation merely lagged, and more often tied to nutrient, mixed-community and iron conditions.

truly_dark_genes--92c362cf.gist: Re-annotating Fitness Browser dark genes with a modern annotation tool gave a more informative label to most of those linked to pangenomes, shrinking the mystery set to a small core that both old and new annotations still call hypothetical proteins.

truly_dark_genes--947aec4f.gist: Genes that stay unexplained after modern annotation are shorter, more often found only in some strains, and have orthologs in far fewer organisms than genes whose function was simply slow to be annotated. Only 29.3% of the truly dark genes have orthologs.

truly_dark_genes--ba47a194.gist: Of the truly dark genes that remain unexplained after modern annotation, only 246 have no clue of any kind. Most carry sequence identifiers alone, and many others have a fitness or essentiality signal, which gives a starting map for choosing genes to study.

truly_dark_genes--d1b84273.gist: Genes that stay unannotated even with modern tools cluster in a few organisms: Methanococcus strains S2 and JJ hold 55% of all truly dark genes in the Fitness Browser, with archaea at the high end, likely reflecting sparse archaeal coverage in annotation databases.
